# korean-word-of-the-day — a static resting screen showing one Korean word per day and a Korean word clock

## What it is

This repo is a static web page for a wall panel, tablet, or spare monitor. It renders two views: a Korean word of the day and a Korean word clock. The word of the day shows Hangul, romanization, pronunciation, meaning, syllables, and an example sentence. The word clock lights a letter grid spelling the current time as a spoken Korean phrase.

The entire product is two static files: `index.html` and `words.js`. There is no build step, no API, no tokens, no network calls, and no tracking. Opening `index.html` in a browser is the whole deployment. The word rotation is deterministic by local calendar date, and a specific date can pin a specific word.

The word bank lives in a global `window.KOREAN_WORDS` array inside `words.js`. Each entry includes Korean text, romanization, pronunciation, part of speech, meaning, syllables, and example sentences. The first word is 설레다, ensuring day one matches the approved mockup. The data shape mirrors exactly what the Resting Screen design renders, so adding a word is data-only and never a layout change.

## Why it exists

The product provides a resting screen with Korean language content for a wall panel, tablet, or spare monitor. It works offline because it makes no network calls. The word rotation is deterministic by date, so the same date always shows the same word.

## How it is used

- **Owner:** opens `index.html` in a browser, or points a kiosk browser at the file or the repo's GitHub Pages URL at 1280×800 or similar.
- **Agent:** runs `node tests/test_korean_pin.js` to test the date-pin logic.
- **Automatic consumers:** none — the page makes no network calls and has no API.

## Boundaries

- **Owns:** the word bank (`window.KOREAN_WORDS`), the date-based word rotation, the word clock view, and the date-pin logic.
- **Never does:** make network calls — the page must work with the internet down; fetch data from an API — there is no API; require a build step — it is two static files.
- **Escalates to owner:** any change to the word bank's data shape, because the shape mirrors exactly what the Resting Screen design renders.
- **Owner:** `UNKNOWN (fact not harvested)`.
